summary: Craig advances a cumulative theistic inference; Krauss counters that natural alternatives, evidential uncertainty, secular morality, and ordinary history prevent decisive discrimination.

pro.text: evidence is much broader than what science tells us
pro.context: Craig broadens admissible evidence beyond science to include moral experience, metaphysics, history, and other features of human experience.

con.text: it's not God that chose what's moral
con.context: Krauss argues that moral wrongness remaining fixed despite divine approval would make morality independent of divine choice.

pro-cumulative-probability-standard.words: Facts about cosmic origins, order, morality, and history jointly increase the probability of God relative to the same background information without those facts.
pro-cumulative-probability-standard.critique: Strongest feature: The move establishes a precise comparative-probability framework, identifies several evidential domains, and connects their cumulative relevance directly to the motion rather than claiming that any isolated consideration deductively proves theism. Principal limitation: The assertion that the probability increase is indisputable outruns the presentation because neither evidential independence nor an aggregation method, background prior, or comparative likelihood is supplied for the announced considerations. Live burden: The cumulative case must demonstrate that its components remain independently informative, survive the strongest natural alternatives, and jointly favor theism without repeatedly counting the same explanatory intuition. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional motion-level relevance, explicit qualification, stable terminology, and coherent evidential architecture, moderated by incomplete probabilistic warrant and implicit cumulative bridges.

pro-contingency-necessary-cause.words: Contingent beings require explanation either through their own nature or an external cause, and the universe therefore points toward a necessarily existing transcendent ground.
pro-contingency-necessary-cause.critique: Strongest feature: The move presents a recoverable explanatory principle, distinguishes necessary existence from externally caused contingency, and applies that distinction directly to the universe and the affirmative cosmological route. Principal limitation: The reasoning reaches a necessary explanatory terminus more readily than it identifies that terminus with a transcendent divine person, while the governing explanatory principle is asserted without comparison against natural necessary candidates. Live burden: The argument must establish both that the relevant totality is contingent and that a specifically divine ground has explanatory advantages unavailable to a necessary physical structure, law, or multiverse. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes clear logical organization, substantial responsiveness to the central burden, and a disciplined proposition, while preserving the material identification gap and comparatively limited evidential warrant.

pro-cosmic-beginning-cause.words: Whatever begins to exist has a cause; the universe began to exist, so its cause transcends physical space and time and supports theism.
pro-cosmic-beginning-cause.critique: Strongest feature: The move states a compact causal syllogism whose premises, conclusion, and relevance are readily recoverable, then clearly explains why a cause of physical spacetime would not itself be spatial or temporal. Principal limitation: Even if the causal conclusion follows, the move compresses the further transition from a transcendent cause to God and does not yet address competing interpretations of a cosmic boundary or beginning. Live burden: The affirmative must defend the universe's finite past across applicable cosmological models and show why the inferred cause possesses distinctively theistic rather than merely nonclassical causal properties. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects excellent burden contact, coherent structure, and substantial scientific-philosophical relevance, tempered by the underdeveloped divine identification and incomplete engagement with alternative cosmologies.

pro-fine-tuning-design.words: Life-permitting constants and quantities invite comparison among physical necessity, chance, and design, with design offered as the superior explanation.
pro-fine-tuning-design.critique: Strongest feature: The move organizes the fine-tuning dispute around explicit competing explanations, identifies the alleged independence of constants from known laws, and advances a directly relevant comparative inference rather than a bare expression of wonder. Principal limitation: The design preference lacks stated priors, likelihoods, and a sufficiently specified design hypothesis, while independence from currently known laws does not establish independence from every deeper physical account. Live burden: The affirmative must compare design against dynamical generation, multiverse selection, and observational conditioning under defensible probability measures rather than treating the initial trilemma as automatically exhaustive. Locked score: The strong and competent band rewards clear alternatives, strong relevance, and charitable attention to necessity and chance, while retaining significant reservations about calibration, exhaustiveness, and quantitative warrant.

pro-objective-morality-ground.words: Some acts are objectively wrong, and objective moral values and duties allegedly require God because atheism cannot furnish their ontological foundation.
pro-objective-morality-ground.critique: Strongest feature: The move sharply distinguishes moral objectivity from personal preference, supplies vivid examples of apparent objective wrongness, and connects the claimed moral facts to a central theistic grounding argument. Principal limitation: The inference from objective wrongness to God's existence is insufficiently defended, distinctions among values, duties, and ontology become unstable, and the certainty-level probability claim radically exceeds the presented dependence premise. Live burden: The affirmative must show why secular realism, rational normativity, or other nondivine moral ontologies fail, while explaining how divine nature grounds authority without circularity or arbitrariness. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct relevance and a recognizable syllogistic structure, but its lower boundary preserves substantial penalties for overstatement, incomplete warrant, and limited representation of serious secular alternatives.

pro-resurrection-core-facts.words: The empty tomb, postmortem appearances, and transformed disciples constitute historical facts that Craig argues are best explained by Jesus's divine resurrection.
pro-resurrection-core-facts.critique: Strongest feature: The move supplies a concrete three-part historical dataset, identifies resurrection as a comparative explanation, and makes the route testable against recognizable historical alternatives rather than relying only on confessional affirmation. Principal limitation: The asserted degree of scholarly agreement, independence of the traditions, and reliability of each alleged fact remain insufficiently developed, while acceptance of the dataset does not independently establish a miraculous explanation. Live burden: The case must justify the sources, transmission, dating, and dependence behind every core fact and compare resurrection with both individual and composite ordinary hypotheses using priors as well as explanatory scope. Locked score: The strong and competent band credits clear structure, high relevance, and a substantive abductive case, while retaining reservations about historical warrant, implicit qualifications, and the extraordinary explanatory leap.

con-affirmative-empirical-burden.words: Craig bears the affirmative burden to provide recognizable empirical evidence for God, whereas Krauss need not establish that no God exists.
con-affirmative-empirical-burden.critique: Strongest feature: The move correctly locates the affirmative burden, distinguishes failure to establish the motion from disproving God, and directly tests whether Craig's cumulative considerations genuinely discriminate in favor of the proposed conclusion. Principal limitation: Recognizable empirical evidence is never given a stable criterion, and the presentation sometimes suggests a scientific restriction broad enough to exclude legitimate philosophical, moral, or historical evidence without defending that exclusion. Live burden: The negative must articulate a defensible evidential standard that demands discrimination and testability where appropriate while permitting nonlaboratory reasoning capable of supporting metaphysical conclusions. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects clear burden allocation, direct responsiveness, and important methodological pressure, moderated by uncertain scope, incomplete justification of empirical exclusivity, and vulnerability to the self-defeat objection.

con-extraordinary-divine-evidence-standa.words: An infinitely powerful divine intelligence is extraordinarily antecedently demanding, so ordinary probability assertions require exceptionally discriminating supporting evidence.
con-extraordinary-divine-evidence-standa.critique: Strongest feature: The move appropriately connects an extraordinary divine hypothesis with a heightened evidential demand and challenges whether merely asserting probability increases supplies enough discrimination over comparatively ordinary alternatives. Principal limitation: The slogan remains quantitatively implicit and occasionally treats extraordinary evidence as though it must look spectacular, when the relevant requirement is strong likelihood discrimination relative to a suitably specified prior. Live burden: The negative must explain how its standard operates without assuming the contested improbability of theism and must evaluate whether multiple modest considerations can cumulatively satisfy a demanding Bayesian threshold. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes direct contact with Craig's evidential framework, clear conceptual force, and rational sensitivity to priors, while reserving judgment because the threshold, comparison class, and evidential metric remain underdeveloped.

con-infinity-intuition-challenge.words: Mathematics and successful physics routinely use infinities, so counterintuitive examples alone cannot establish that an actual infinite cosmic past is impossible.
con-infinity-intuition-challenge.critique: Strongest feature: The reply usefully challenges any inference from intuitive oddity to impossibility and invokes mathematics and empirically successful physics as disciplined contexts in which infinite quantities can be handled consistently. Principal limitation: The discussion shifts among mathematical sets, series, physical quantities, singular behavior, and an actually instantiated temporal history, so success with one category does not establish the physical possibility of another. Live burden: The negative must address the specific metaphysical and cosmological arguments against an actual past infinity while distinguishing formal mathematical coherence from physical realization and temporal traversal. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects a relevant and intellectually serious correction to intuition-based reasoning, moderated by partly unstable terminology, limited model-specific evidence, and incomplete contact with actual temporal instantiation.

con-contingency-gap-objection.words: Unknown explanations and contingent causal processes invite further physical investigation rather than an inference that their still-undiscovered explanation is God.
con-contingency-gap-objection.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies the unsupported transition from explanatory ignorance to a divine conclusion, while recommending investigation and acknowledging that an account may be entirely physical. Principal limitation: It narrows the affirmative’s argument about contingent reality into a claim about unknown processes producing human beings, so its warning against gap reasoning does not directly defeat the principle demanding an ultimate explanation. Live burden: The negative must isolate the divine-identification gap even if that explanatory principle is granted, then explain how a physical terminus could meet the relevant modal requirement. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects central diagnostic pressure, disciplined uncertainty, and relevance, tempered by target slippage, limited warrant, and no developed natural necessary-ground account.

con-eternal-multiverse-first-cause-alter.words: Inflation, quantum gravity, and a potentially eternal multiverse allow our observable universe to arise naturally without requiring a relevant divine first cause.
con-eternal-multiverse-first-cause-alter.critique: Strongest feature: The move presents concrete physical model classes, distinguishes our observable universe from a wider multiverse, and acknowledges uncertainty while showing how a local cosmic beginning need not immediately imply divine causation. Principal limitation: A multiverse capable of generating our region blocks only the local first-cause inference unless its own past-eternity or boundary conditions are independently established, and physical motivation alone does not settle ultimate contingency. Live burden: The negative must show that the proposed wider structure is genuinely past-eternal or otherwise dissolves the relevant causal demand, while avoiding conversion of speculative possibility into established probability. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, disciplined modal calibration, stable distinctions, and a scientifically motivated alternative, with residual limitations concerning the multiverse's own origin and modal status.

con-moral-independence-dilemma.words: If grave wrongdoing remains wrong despite divine approval, moral truth constrains God and cannot originate merely in God's discretionary commands.
con-moral-independence-dilemma.critique: Strongest feature: The move formulates a sharp counterfactual test that exposes arbitrariness in unconstrained divine-command theories and clearly explains why fixed moral truth would be independent of divine choice. Principal limitation: The dilemma directly defeats voluntarism more readily than a necessary-divine-nature theory, which denies that contrary commands are genuinely possible and relocates rather than simply accepts the authority question. Live burden: The negative must show that appealing to God's essential character either remains explanatorily circular or fails to improve upon independent moral realism, without representing necessary-character accounts as discretionary command theories. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise recoverability, excellent diagnostic relevance, well-matched asserted force, and a powerful objection, with only the nature-based response and its residual authority problem left for further comparison.

pro-beginning-infinity-quantum-defense.words: Formal uses of infinity and quantum-vacuum cosmology do not establish an eternal physical past, while cosmological boundary results support a beginning.
pro-beginning-infinity-quantum-defense.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly contacts both principal objections, distinguishes formal mathematical infinity from physical temporal instantiation, and invokes a relevant cosmological theorem instead of resting entirely on intuition. Principal limitation: The theorem's applicability conditions and the meaning of geodesic incompleteness remain implicit, while proof-level rhetoric exceeds what a result conditional on average expansion establishes across quantum-gravity models. Live burden: The affirmative must specify which cosmologies satisfy the theorem, explain what its boundary licenses ontologically, and show that possible extensions do not preserve an eternal relevant physical history. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects strong responsiveness, useful conceptual distinctions, and important scientific engagement, moderated by overstated universality, incomplete theorem qualification, and an unresolved transition from boundary evidence to divine causation.

con-physical-fine-tuning-alternatives.words: Quantum-gravitational origins, variable physical laws, and observer selection offer physical routes to apparent fine-tuning without supernatural imposition.
con-physical-fine-tuning-alternatives.critique: Strongest feature: The move supplies several concrete natural alternative classes, emphasizes observer selection, and uses the broader phenomenon of naturally generated apparent design to challenge a premature inference from suitability to purpose. Principal limitation: Biological selection and cosmological observational selection are partly blended, and listing possible mechanisms does not furnish a likelihood comparison explaining the complete distribution of constants or initial conditions. Live burden: The negative must specify a generating model, probability measure, and selection effect capable of making the observed life-permitting conditions materially less surprising than they are under the relevant design hypothesis. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes direct responsiveness, calibrated possibility claims, and meaningful physical alternatives, while preserving substantial limitations in quantitative warrant, model specificity, and the reach of the evolutionary analogy.

pro-multiverse-fine-tuning-defense.words: Bare many-worlds proposals neither predict embodied interactive observers nor explain the apparently special laws governing the world-generating mechanism itself.
pro-multiverse-fine-tuning-defense.critique: Strongest feature: The reply identifies two distinct explanatory deficits: observer selection alone may not predict embodied interactive observers, and a multiverse generator may relocate fine-tuning into its higher-level laws rather than eliminate it. Principal limitation: The criticism addresses broadly described model classes and does not establish that every multiverse measure, generating dynamic, or observer distribution fails, much less that design consequently becomes the preferred explanation. Live burden: The affirmative must formulate the relevant multiverse alternatives at their strongest, show that their measures or dynamics require comparable fine-tuning, and then conduct an explicit likelihood comparison with design. Locked score: The very strong band reflects excellent responsiveness, precise explanatory questions, and forceful pressure on underspecified alternatives, tempered by incomplete model coverage and the absence of a positive quantitative design comparison.

pro-necessary-divine-character.words: Divine commands necessarily express God's compassionate, just, and fair character, while naturalism allegedly lacks any foundation for objective moral duties.
pro-necessary-divine-character.critique: Strongest feature: The response directly answers the arbitrariness counterfactual by locating commands in an essential divine character and clearly denies that grave wrongdoing could become permissible through a contrary decree. Principal limitation: Necessary character blocks arbitrary commands but does not independently explain why that character is morally authoritative, and the renewed assertion that naturalism lacks objective values receives little comparative argument. Live burden: The affirmative must provide a noncircular grounding relation between divine essence and moral authority while showing why secular realism cannot furnish equivalent normativity without a personal commander. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes a complete and responsive answer to simple voluntarism, stable distinctions, and central relevance, moderated by the residual authority problem and underdeveloped dismissal of naturalistic moral ontology.

con-natural-moral-understanding.words: Rationality, evolution, biology, and inquiry can substantially explain moral understanding and conduct without belief in God, although the account remains incomplete.
con-natural-moral-understanding.critique: Strongest feature: The move offers plausible natural contributors to moral cognition, accurately notes that nonbelievers can behave morally, and explicitly acknowledges that the proposed explanation remains incomplete rather than claiming a finished theory. Principal limitation: Explanations of moral motivation, learning, and behavior do not by themselves answer the affirmative's ontological question concerning objective moral truth, and those distinct targets are not consistently separated. Live burden: The negative must connect its account of moral competence to a defensible secular ontology or explain why the motion requires no such ontology before the theistic grounding inference can succeed. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects appropriate humility, empirical relevance, and meaningful partial contact, moderated by incomplete responsiveness to objective grounding and instability among understanding, conduct, motivation, and truth.

con-dynamical-fine-tuning-and-purpose.words: Dynamics explain some alleged fine-tuning, while unresolved vacuum energy is not shown life-essential and cosmic inefficiency weighs against competent purposive design.
con-dynamical-fine-tuning-and-purpose.critique: Strongest feature: The move distinguishes dynamically explained initial conditions from unresolved parameters, questions whether vacuum energy is genuinely necessary for life, and tests competent-purpose hypotheses against apparent cosmic inefficiency. Principal limitation: The local physical cautions expand into a categorical denial of purpose or design that exceeds acknowledged uncertainty, while apparent inefficiency depends upon assumptions about what a possible designer intended to optimize. Live burden: The negative must identify which fine-tuning claims existing dynamics actually explain and show how the remaining observations compare under specified natural and purposive hypotheses without treating ignorance as disproof. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects substantive scientific engagement, direct comparative relevance, and several targeted rebuttals, moderated by overbroad conclusions, purpose-dependent assumptions, and incomplete coverage of the full parameter set.

con-resurrection-testimony-error.words: Fallible human testimony is antecedently more plausible than miracle, so resurrection reports require source-specific reliability before supporting God.
con-resurrection-testimony-error.critique: Strongest feature: The reply properly introduces ordinary testimonial fallibility and prior plausibility into the historical comparison, directly challenging any automatic transition from reported experiences to a supernatural event. Principal limitation: Labeling the material anecdotal and invoking generic human error does not analyze these sources' dating, dependence, transmission, incentives, or particular reliability, so it cannot independently resolve the disputed reports. Live burden: The negative must develop a source-specific error model capable of explaining the principal traditions while comparing its explanatory scope and evidential probability with the resurrection hypothesis. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes coherent probabilistic pressure, high relevance, and a readily understood ordinary alternative, moderated by limited historical detail, compressed characterization of the evidence, and incomplete engagement with the affirmative's multi-fact comparative case.

con-ordinary-resurrection-explanations.words: Imagination, illusion, human error, or deliberate enhancement are ordinary and therefore initially more plausible explanations than supernatural resurrection.
con-ordinary-resurrection-explanations.critique: Strongest feature: The move presents several recognizable ordinary explanation classes, appropriately emphasizes their prior plausibility, and explicitly refrains from pretending that any particular alternative has been established as historical fact. Principal limitation: A disjunction of possible mechanisms is not yet a unified explanation of the empty tomb, appearances, and transformed belief, and no single or composite model is tested against all three alleged facts. Live burden: The negative must construct the strongest historically plausible combination of ordinary mechanisms and compare its source fit, independence assumptions, explanatory scope, and priors with resurrection. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects careful calibration, clear alternatives, and meaningful contact with the miraculous inference, moderated by partial responsiveness, limited evidential development, and failure to supply a complete rival explanation.

pro-resurrection-comparative-explanation.words: Conspiracy, apparent death, and hallucination theories allegedly fail explanatory scope, power, plausibility, and non-ad-hocness compared with resurrection.
pro-resurrection-comparative-explanation.critique: Strongest feature: The reply names major historical alternatives, evaluates them using explicit abductive criteria, and directly answers both generic testimonial error and the demand for an ordinary explanation covering the proposed facts. Principal limitation: Low scholarly adherence and a list of explanatory criteria do not establish that every natural rival fails, especially when composite hypotheses and the exceptionally low prior assigned to miracles remain outside the comparison. Live burden: The affirmative must compare the strongest combined natural account with resurrection using source-specific likelihoods, explanatory scope, complexity, and antecedent probability rather than dismissing classic theories collectively. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects excellent responsiveness, clear comparative structure, and central relevance, tempered by material overstatement, incomplete priors, and limited charity toward composite ordinary explanations.

pro-necessary-terminus.words: Explanation stops non-arbitrarily with a being necessary by nature, whereas contingent entities require external causes; Craig identifies that terminus as God.
pro-necessary-terminus.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly answers the arbitrariness objection, clearly distinguishes necessary from contingent existence, and explains how an ultimate terminus could satisfy rather than violate the proposed explanatory principle. Principal limitation: The move stipulates that God occupies the necessary category without independently demonstrating divine necessity or showing why the universe, laws, or another natural structure cannot occupy it instead. Live burden: The affirmative must defend the modal status of God and establish a principled comparative advantage over natural necessary candidates rather than securing the conclusion through definition. Locked score: The strong and competent band recognizes coherent termination rules, very high responsiveness, and direct central relevance, moderated by limited evidential warrant, incomplete engagement with natural termini, and an unresolved identification bridge.

con-natural-necessary-terminus.words: An always-existing, physically motivated multiverse can serve as a natural explanatory terminus unless God has a demonstrated modal advantage over it.
con-natural-necessary-terminus.critique: Strongest feature: The reply squarely exposes the identification burden by proposing a structurally parallel natural terminus and asking what demonstrated advantage distinguishes divine necessity from a physically motivated multiverse. Principal limitation: It partly conflates temporal eternity with metaphysical necessity, because defining a multiverse as always existing does not show that it exists by its own nature or could not have failed to exist. Live burden: The negative must match the modal property claimed for God or explain why merely supplying a live eternal physical alternative is sufficient to defeat the affirmative inference. Locked score: The strong and competent band reflects direct responsiveness, a valuable parity challenge, and strong central relevance, moderated by unstable modal terminology, stipulative reasoning, and limited evidence that the multiverse is genuinely necessary.

pro-broad-evidence-scope.words: Scientific evidence is one rational domain among moral experience, philosophy, metaphysics, and history, all of which may contribute to a cumulative theistic inference.
pro-broad-evidence-scope.critique: Strongest feature: The reply clearly distinguishes several evidential domains, diagnoses strict scientific verification as self-defeating, and restores the affirmative's cumulative moral, historical, philosophical, and scientific case to direct motion-level relevance. Principal limitation: Krauss's position may demand unusually strong empirical discrimination without endorsing exclusive scientism, and establishing broad admissibility does not show that each admitted consideration actually favors theism. Live burden: The affirmative must engage the narrower evidential challenge charitably and demonstrate the comparative force of every cited domain instead of moving from admissibility to explanatory success. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, stable terminology, broad argumentative scope, and a powerful epistemic correction, moderated by possible overstatement of the opposing standard and incomplete warrant for theism's claimed explanatory power.

strengths: Established a coherent probability-raising framework that connected every affirmative route to the motion.
Presented clear, recoverable constructive arguments across contingency, cosmic origins, fine-tuning, morality, and resurrection.
Answered multiverse objections by pressing both observer prediction and higher-level fine-tuning of generating laws.
Broadened the evidential framework effectively by distinguishing scientific evidence from moral, philosophical, metaphysical, and historical considerations.
Responded directly to arbitrariness and ordinary-history objections with necessary-character and comparative-explanation accounts.

blunders.text: The moral argument assigned certainty-level force without establishing that objective morality uniquely requires God.
Several cosmological moves reached a necessary or transcendent terminus more readily than they identified that terminus as God.
The resurrection comparison did not fully incorporate composite ordinary hypotheses or explicit prior probabilities.

strengths: Correctly placed the burden of establishing evidence on the affirmative without assuming an obligation to disprove every God concept.
Supplied concrete natural alternatives from quantum gravity, inflation, multiverse cosmology, dynamics, and observer selection.
Delivered a particularly strong moral-independence dilemma against unconstrained divine-command accounts.
Introduced prior probability and ordinary testimonial fallibility into the resurrection comparison.
Repeatedly treated unresolved physical questions as grounds for investigation rather than premature supernatural conclusions.

blunders.text: The infinity response moved too freely between formal mathematical infinity and an actually instantiated temporal past.
The natural necessary-terminus reply conflated an eternal multiverse with a metaphysically necessary reality.
Natural moral cognition and conduct were developed more fully than a secular ontology of objective moral truth.
The ordinary resurrection alternatives lacked a unified, source-specific account of all the affirmative's proposed facts.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain coherence test
newArguments.text: A cumulative case gains force when one independently specified hypothesis predicts patterns across domains without being repeatedly modified to fit each observation. Theism could therefore be tested for cross-domain coherence: whether the same account of a rational, morally perfect, purposive ground generates expectations concerning intelligible laws, conscious reasoners, normative obligations, and historically meaningful action. This does not assume independence or guarantee success. It creates a disciplined comparison against a naturalistic package whose separate components may also combine coherently but incur their own complexity and coordination costs.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new model-comparison test based on cross-domain coherence and coordination costs.

newArguments.title: Modal profile comparison
newArguments.text: The contingency dispute can be improved by comparing modal profiles rather than labels. A candidate terminus should explain why contingent reality exists, why the governing structure has its particular capacities, and why the terminus is not merely temporally everlasting but noncontingent. A personal ground would gain an advantage only if agency explains the selection of contingent structures without importing equal unexplained complexity. A natural terminus would gain an advantage if its necessity follows from a credible theory. This framework prevents both sides from defining their preferred terminus into victory.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the shared tendency to stipulate rather than demonstrate the terminus's modal status.

newArguments.title: Evidential dependence audit
newArguments.text: The cumulative case may overstate its force if several observations arise from the same deeper facts or interpretive commitments. Cosmic beginning and contingency may share assumptions about ultimate explanation; moral experience and perceived purpose may share human agency-detection tendencies; resurrection judgments may depend upon prior openness to miracle. A formal dependence audit would group correlated evidence, test conclusions under alternative priors, and prevent repeated counting. If support for theism remains stable after those adjustments, it is stronger; if it collapses, apparent breadth was not equivalent to independent confirmation.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new sensitivity analysis for dependence and correlated evidential interpretation.

newArguments.title: Symmetric specification principle
newArguments.text: Comparative explanation should require equal specificity from divine and natural hypotheses. A vague designer can accommodate almost any constants, moral order, or historical outcome, just as an unspecified multiverse can accommodate almost any universe. Both sides should state mechanisms, probability distributions, scope, and potential disconfirming observations at comparable resolution. Penalizing only natural models for missing details while allowing flexible divine intentions would distort the comparison; penalizing only theism while accepting an undefined multiverse would do the same. Symmetric specification makes the dispute more rigorous without presupposing either conclusion.

novelty.explanation: This repairs asymmetric model criticism by imposing the same specification burden on both sides.
